newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat to Paris for talks on peace.
newsitem.headline: Arafat to Paris for talks on peace.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat will hold "important" talks with French President Jacques Chirac on Monday on a possible role for France in breaking the impasse in peace negotiations with Israel, a PLO official said.
Arafat left self-ruled Gaza for Paris early on Monday.
"President Arafat has been invited at a short notice by President Chirac for important talks on the peace process," a senior PLO official said.

"The Europeans have asked France to play a leading role in breaking the impasse in the peace process and to coordinate with the United States to return to play a role in solving the crisis," said the official, who insisted on anonymity.
Formal PLO-Israeli peace moves came to a halt in March after Israel broke ground for a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

A U.S. peace envoy failed in April to restart the talks. Egypt stepped in and PLO officials said Cairo would continue to mediate between the sides despite its failure to persuade Israel to suspend settlement building for six months.
Israel has welcomed Egyptian mediation but it has traditionally resisted European involvement in its peace moves with the PLO.

Officials said the United States was preparing to return to present ideas to restart the deadlocked talks, but only after all mediation efforts were exhausted and when the sides were ready to make compromises.
